title: The License Plate Reader Put Your Car Three Blocks From the Scene
summary: A sponsored/business-wire explainer on how Flock Safety ALPR hits are being used as probable cause in criminal investigations, warning drivers not to make voluntary statements and outlining defense strategies. It notes courts have largely allowed warrantless ALPR queries and cites reporting on officer misuse of Flock to track personal targets.

key_quotes.quote: An ALPR reads a plate as a vehicle passes a fixed point. It logs the plate, the timestamp, and the location of the camera. That is the entire data point.

Courts have largely blessed warrantless queries of these databases so far, and a Brennan Center analysis has noted that aggregated ALPR histories can chronicle a driver's movements in a way the Supreme Court once found troubling for cell-site data.
Reporting over the past year has documented officers using Flock to track romantic partners and other personal targets hundreds of times, in cases that ended in resignations and criminal charges.
